recipient_note: Demo letter sealed to the single-purpose testnet account's own registered ML-KEM-1024 key. A letter to oneself is a personal commitment; it exercises the same seal, commit, lock and release path as a letter to another person.
content: Demo, non-personal text. Recovered after release: "Demo letter on QoreChain Diana testnet: this note stayed sealed until its opening time. Hello from Future Post!" (sha256 c1ef8ec871b08b9bdad6fb33eb834c65d22605b65d9a72714836281410a29561)
built_with: src/split-envelope.js encryptLetter (AES-256-GCM, content key split A XOR B)
src/qoreseal-adapter.js sealShareA (QoreSeal ML-KEM-1024 to the on-chain registered key)

register.note: registerLetter passed the pqcKeyStatus guard (sender registered, algorithm 1, possession proven)

early_release_check: Before the opening time a read-only simulation of releaseShareB (eth_call) was refused at chain time 1795688474 (unlock 1795688645).

release.note: sent once chain time passed the opening time; ShareBReleased event emitted

open_after_release.how: The recipient's QoreSeal key opened sealed share A; combined with share B read from the ShareBReleased event it decrypted the ciphertext. The recipient secret key is private and not in this repository.

read_only_verification: npm run verify:diana-letter (eth_call / receipts only, all checks true at block time of verification)

explorer.note: Open with the explorer switched to Testnet.

scope: One demo letter registered and released on FuturePostReleaseV2 on testnet. Recipient binding is an opaque hash; V2 checks the sender key only. This is a single-account demo, not a two-device test. v1 is unchanged.
